headline: Saudi Arabia strikes Yemen capital Sanaa as Houthis threaten oil facilities, escalating conflict
summary: Saudi Arabia launched strikes on Yemen's capital Sanaa, prompting Houthi threats of "harsh and painful" retaliation against Saudi oil sites, including Aramco's headquarters. This marks a significant escalation in the ongoing conflict.
details: Saudi Arabia struck Yemen's capital Sanaa on Tuesday, targeting a fuel depot on the outskirts, according to Houthi media. This comes as the Iran-aligned Houthi group threatened retaliation against Saudi oil facilities, signaling a rapid escalation of the war.
Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree warned of a "harsh and painful" response to any strikes on Sanaa. Possible targets named include Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran and an oil refinery in Riyadh.

The group also renewed warnings to oil workers in Saudi Arabia to stay away from sites it might attack. Saudi Arabia's cabinet, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, stated that the Houthis would face consequences for their repeated attacks.

This escalation follows a Houthi ballistic missile strike on Riyadh airport on Saturday, which reportedly killed 13 people. Further attacks have grounded flights across Saudi Arabia, coinciding with a major energy conference hosted by the kingdom.

Yemen's civil war reignited last month after Houthis made rapid gains along the Red Sea coast towards the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait. This strait is crucial for Saudi and global energy shipments, especially since Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz earlier this year.

Saudi Arabia has sought increased support from allies to counter Houthi missile and drone attacks. Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan pledged Ankara's support, and US President Donald Trump told reporters the Houthis were "behaving very badly."

Washington, however, has so far resisted direct involvement in the conflict against the Houthis. Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi reiterated Tehran's willingness to mediate between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi group.

headline_marked: [[Tk 23.5 crore medical equipment unused]] at Faridpur Medical College Hospital, ACC finds
headline: Tk 23.5 crore medical equipment unused at Faridpur Medical College Hospital, ACC finds
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) found that a Cath Lab installed nine years ago remains inoperative, and a Linear Accelerator is still in its packaging, leading to a significant waste of public funds.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has reported that approximately BDT 23.5 crore was squandered on the purchase of two medical devices that remain unused at Faridpur Medical College Hospital.

This revelation came from Md. Mostafiz, Assistant Director of the ACC District Integrated Office, during a press conference held on Tuesday night, following a two-day operation that began on Monday morning.

Among the unused equipment, a Cath Lab installed nine years ago has never been operational. Additionally, a Linear Accelerator is still found in its original packaging, never having been put into service.
The ACC also uncovered information regarding irregularities and mismanagement in the procurement of Medical, Surgical, and Research (MSR) items at the hospital.

According to ACC officials, the operation was conducted under directives from the headquarters, prompted by allegations of patient harassment, referral of patients to private clinics and diagnostic centers through touts, and irregularities in outsourcing appointments.
